positions.name: Scorpio Tankers Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/11 (Friday) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.driver: Tier 2: 9/3 time charters fixed at $40,188-$42,500/day, Q3 LR2 TCE guided $64,900/day, product-tanker leverage to refined-product disruption
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE PRODUCT-TANKER EXPRESSION, AND THE ONLY TANKER NAME WITH HARD CONTRACTED DAY-RATE NUMBERS RATHER THAN A SENTIMENT STORY: on 9/3 Scorpio Tankers disclosed time charter agreements for three product tankers - STI Gladiator and STI Jermyn for three years at $40,188 and $42,500 per day respectively, both commencing in September, and STI Pontiac for three years at $23,900 per day from Q4 - and in the same release gave preliminary Q3 average daily time charter equivalent rates of $64,900 for LR2 vessels, $30,000 for MR and $25,500 for Handymax. Those are contracted, disclosed, company-verified numbers, not a war-risk narrative, and they are the reason this is the tanker I want alongside the crude-carrier exposure this book already holds in FRO. The mechanism matters: the Houthi strikes hit Saudi Aramco facilities at Abha, Najran and Jazan - REFINING and export infrastructure - which disrupts refined-product supply faster than crude availability, and it is product tankers, not VLCCs, that carry the replacement barrels on longer routes when Gulf product flows are rerouted. Scorpio trades at 4.67x trailing earnings and 1.17x book with a 2.16% dividend, the cheapest multiple of anything in this book, and its 8/17 ex-dividend date has passed. It is quoted at 83.66 against an 83.06 close and sits 4.3% below its 87.39 52-week high from 5/5/2026, so unlike CVX and TNK I am not paying for a fresh high.
positions.risks: THE NAMED CATALYST IS A WEEK OLD - the charter disclosure is dated 9/3 and the market has had five sessions to price it, so what I am actually buying today is sector correlation with a stale company release attached. I should be explicit about that. Volume of 640K on 9/9 ran only 0.91x its 702K 30-day average, so this is not a name being accumulated, and on a 43.2M float with a $4.16B market cap it is thin enough that a single institutional seller sets the price. Tanker equities are the most violently mean-reverting group in the market - spot rates can halve inside a fortnight and the equities front-run both directions - so a 4.67x multiple is a mid-cycle illusion rather than a valuation floor, and the very fact that it is the cheapest thing in this book should be read as the market pricing rate normalisation rather than as a bargain. Scorpio is Monaco-domiciled with 24 employees and an externally managed structure, which is a governance and related-party profile this book would not accept in any other sector. It has run from 48.93 on 1/2/2026 to 83.66, a 71% move in eight months. This is the second of four Transportation names taking that sector to its cap, and FRO, STNG, TNK and INSW all fail together on a single de-escalation headline. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/11 (Friday) or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.driver: Tier 2: Muse agentic AI launch, +6.6% on 9/9 on 2.11x volume, +1.25% follow-through pre-market
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE ONLY BREAKOUT IN LARGE-CAP TECHNOLOGY AND THE HEAVIEST VOLUME CONFIRMATION IN THIS BOOK: Meta rose 6.6% on 9/9 on 35.90M shares against a 17.04M 30-day average - 2.11x relative volume - opening at 648.29, running to 657.86 and closing at 653.69 in the upper half of its range. It is quoted at 661.89 this morning, +1.25%, on a tight 661.58/662.00 market. The named catalyst is the launch of Muse, Meta's agentic AI application, and the specific thing the market repriced is the transaction capability: speaking on CNBC on Wednesday, T. Rowe Price Science and Technology Fund manager Tony Wang argued Meta holds a structural distribution advantage in what he called the 'battle of the agents' because it can push agents across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp with user context attached, and that unlike a conventional LLM which researches and then hands the user off, Muse can negotiate and, with permission, COMPLETE purchases. Two-day follow-through on 2.11x volume after a 6.6% move is a materially better tape signature than a one-day pop, and this is the only Technology Services name with a fresh named catalyst on a morning when NVDA, AMD, MU, AVGO, MRVL, PLTR and SMCI are all quoted lower - it is a genuine diversifier from the energy, gold and defence exposure that dominates the rest of the book. At 23.11x earnings Meta is the cheapest mega-cap in this book, cheaper than Apple at 36.25x.
positions.risks: I AM BUYING THE SECOND DAY OF A 6.6% MOVE, WHICH MEANS THE EASY MONEY HAS ALREADY BEEN MADE AND I AM PAYING FOR IT - a fund manager's favourable comments on CNBC are an OPINION, not a booking, an order or a disclosed financial metric, which makes this the lowest-quality catalyst category in today's book alongside ADBE. Muse has no disclosed revenue, no user numbers and no monetisation timeline; agentic commerce that negotiates and completes purchases carries security, fraud and consent exposure that Meta specifically, given its regulatory history, is the worst-positioned large-cap to absorb if something goes wrong. Sell-side is openly split - Rosenblatt raised its target to $886 on 8/27 while Wedbush maintained Neutral at $595 on 9/1, and $595 is 10% BELOW where I am buying. Meta sits 16.3% below its 790.80 52-week high from 9/19/2025, so this is a stock that has spent a year going nowhere and one good session does not change that. Benzinga notes META carries a 9.46%, 8.91% and 8.76% weight in FDN, IGPT and SOCL respectively, so ETF flows will force mechanical selling in any broad technology drawdown regardless of Muse. At 5 shares on a 661.89 price the position is lumpy, and a hot 9/11 CPI that raises September Fed hike odds hits high-multiple technology first. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: RTX Corporation
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/11 open
positions.driver: Tier 2: live US-Iran exchange consuming interceptors, third defence prime, 12.7% below its own 52-week high
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE INTERCEPTOR PRIME IN A CONFLICT THAT IS ACTUALLY CONSUMING INTERCEPTORS: US Central Command has confirmed strikes on Iranian oil tankers, Tehran has fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships, and the Houthis have struck Saudi Aramco facilities at Abha, Najran and Jazan. RTX's Raytheon Missiles and Defense segment supplies the Patriot and Standard Missile families and its Raytheon Intelligence and Space segment the sensors behind them - the specific inventory being drawn down by ship-defence engagements in the Red Sea and the Gulf. RTX is quoted at 198.00 against a 197.55 close, +0.23%, and sits 12.7% below its 226.884 52-week high from 8/10/2026, so unlike the energy names in this book I am buying a name that has already given back ground rather than paying for a fresh high. It is the third defence prime in the book alongside LMT and AVAV, and group-wide participation matters more than any single name moving alone. Overnight only, which is the correct duration for the evidence: this is a headline-correlation position, not a fundamental one.
positions.risks: A +0.23% PRE-MARKET QUOTE IS WEAK CONFIRMATION AND THE 9/9 TAPE WAS WORSE THAN THAT - RTX opened at 199.43, traded DOWN to a 196.80 low and closed at 197.55 in the bottom half of its range, on 3.32M shares against a 3.97M 30-day average (0.84x). Below-average volume into a weak close is not a name being accumulated on a war headline, and I am buying it anyway because the sector is right, which is a thinner reason than this book usually accepts. At 35.01x trailing earnings RTX is the MOST EXPENSIVE defence prime available and roughly double Northrop's multiple - I closed NOC this morning at 16.3x for a small loss and am replacing it with a name at more than twice the valuation. Defence primes are the classic false positive of a geopolitical trade: they spike on the headline and give it back within days because incremental munitions orders take quarters to reach revenue and the US defence budget is set annually regardless of the week's events. Roughly half of RTX is Collins Aerospace and Pratt & Whitney - commercial aerospace, not defence - so a majority of the earnings base has no exposure to the catalyst at all, and Pratt's geared-turbofan powder-metal inspections remain a live cash drag. This is the third Electronic Technology name and takes that sector to its four-name cap alongside LMT. Overnight only.

positions.name: Teekay Tankers Ltd.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/11 open
positions.driver: Tier 2: new 52-week high 97.08 on 9/9 on 1.18x volume, the best volume confirmation of any tanker
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE BEST VOLUME CONFIRMATION IN THE TANKER GROUP AND THE ONLY ONE MAKING A HIGH ON RISING PARTICIPATION: Teekay Tankers closed 9/9 at 96.31 having traded to 97.08 - a new 52-week high set that day - on 604K shares against a 512K 30-day average, 1.18x relative volume. That is the highest relative volume of the four tanker names I priced this morning: FRO ran 1.03x on its breakout, STNG only 0.91x, DHT only 0.83x. It is quoted at 96.75 pre-market, +0.46%. The mechanism is the one actually in the headlines rather than a spillover - CENTCOM confirmed strikes on three Iranian oil tankers and Iran has fired ballistic missiles at US warships, so when tankers themselves are the target, war-risk insurance premia and rerouting away from Hormuz drive ton-mile demand and spot rates directly. Teekay trades at 5.44x earnings and 1.35x book, and its 8/10 ex-dividend date has passed so there is no distribution distortion inside my window. Its mixed crude and product fleet plus the Australian government marine-services contract give it a slightly less pure spot-rate profile than FRO's VLCC-heavy book.
positions.risks: THE QUOTED MARKET IS 85.37 BID / 99.80 OFFER - A 15% SPREAD - WHICH MAKES THIS BY SOME DISTANCE THE WORST-PRICED ENTRY IN TODAY'S BOOK AND I AM FLAGGING IT AS THE PRIMARY RISK RATHER THAN BURYING IT. My 96.75 entry is an actual pre-market print from 10:28Z, not a midpoint, but with a book that wide the realistic fill could be materially worse and the position should be read with that uncertainty attached. It is also why this is overnight-only rather than a swing. The float is just 23.79M shares on a $3.34B market cap - the thinnest float of anything in this book - so a single block trade moves the price several percent in either direction. I am buying at a 52-week high with no overhead support after a run from 47.18 on 10/14/2025 to 97.08, a 106% move in eleven months. Tanker equities mean-revert violently and a 5.44x multiple is a mid-cycle illusion, not a floor. This is the third of four Transportation names, and FRO, STNG, TNK and INSW are one trade expressed four times at roughly 20% of the book - a negotiated de-escalation takes all four down together on the same headline, on the same morning the four Energy Minerals names are also exposed. Overnight only.

positions.name: International Seaways, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/11 open
positions.driver: Tier 2: +1.9% vs the 99.57 dividend-adjusted close, 1.13x volume, 52-week high printed 9/8
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE STRONGEST DIVIDEND-ADJUSTED PRE-MARKET MOVE OF ANY TANKER, WHICH THE HEADLINE QUOTE HIDES: International Seaways goes EX-DIVIDEND TODAY, 9/10, for $5.05 a share. Its raw previous close of 104.62 therefore adjusts to 99.57, and the 101.49 pre-market print at 11:00Z is +1.93% against that adjusted close - the strongest genuine tanker move on the board this morning, roughly four times STNG's and TNK's, and it is invisible unless you make the adjustment. Buying today means I do NOT receive the $5.05, so 101.49 is a clean post-distribution entry with no dividend distortion inside my window. The underlying setup is intact: INSW set a 106.73 52-week high on 9/8 and traded 645K shares on 9/9 against a 573K 30-day average, 1.13x. The mechanism is the same one CENTCOM put in the headlines - confirmed US strikes on three Iranian oil tankers, Iranian ballistic missiles fired at two US Navy warships, and Hormuz flows running below normal - and INSW's split between Crude Tankers and Product Carriers straddles both the crude-rate and the refined-product-rerouting legs. At 6.63x earnings and 2.27x book with an 8.02% trailing yield, it is New York-domiciled and US-listed rather than offshore-structured, which is a genuinely better governance profile than Scorpio's Monaco or Frontline's Cyprus arrangements.
positions.risks: AN 8.02% TRAILING YIELD ON A SHIPPING COMPANY IS A FUNCTION OF PEAK SPOT RATES AND IS NOT DURABLE - the $5.05 quarterly distribution I am explicitly forgoing is variable and set from cash flow, so the yield disappears the moment rates normalise, and the market knows it. Trading ex-dividend introduces real execution ambiguity: pre-market pricing on an ex-date is noisier than usual and my +1.93% read depends entirely on the adjustment being applied correctly, which is a modelling assumption layered on top of a price. The stock made its 106.73 high on 9/8 and then FELL on 9/9, opening at 105.51 and closing at 104.62 - so the most recent full session was a down day, and I am buying a bounce off it. On a 41.49M float at a $5.18B market cap this is thin. It has run from 42.26 on 10/14/2025 to 106.73, a 153% move in eleven months, the most extended chart of the four tankers. This is the FOURTH Transportation name and takes that sector to its cap: FRO, STNG, TNK and INSW are approximately 20% of the book on one variable, and adding the four Energy Minerals names means roughly 40% of this book resolves on whether the Gulf escalates or de-escalates. That is the single largest risk in the account and it is a concentration I am accepting knowingly, not one I have hedged away. Overnight only.

positions.name: Golar LNG Limited
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the 9/11 open
positions.driver: Tier 2: Hormuz carries ~1/5 of global LNG and flows are below normal, FLNG operator, +0.69% pre-market
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 THE FLOATING-LIQUEFACTION LEG OF THE HORMUZ LNG DISRUPTION, AND A MECHANISM THAT DOES NOT FAIL ON THE SAME HEADLINE AS THE CRACK-SPREAD TRADE: the IEA figure being quoted through this episode is that the Strait of Hormuz handles roughly one fifth of global oil AND LNG shipments, and tanker flows through the strait remain below normal. Qatar ships essentially all of its LNG through Hormuz. Golar operates FLNG vessels and floating storage and regasification units - the assets that monetise exactly the situation where fixed onshore liquefaction and conventional shipping routes are disrupted and cargoes need to be liquefied, stored or regasified somewhere other than the planned terminal. Critically, this is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the refining trade that dominates this book: a Gulf de-escalation that crushes crack spreads and takes VLO, PSX and DINO down still leaves LNG contracting economics intact, so this position is not a fourth copy of the same bet. Golar is quoted at 52.30 against a 51.94 close, +0.69%, and sits 9.5% below its 57.79 52-week high from 5/12/2026, so I am buying inside the range rather than paying for a breakout. Its 8/24 ex-dividend date has passed. This is the second of a maximum four Industrial Services names alongside the Cheniere position already held.
positions.risks: VOLUME OF 843,711 ON 9/9 RAN ONLY 0.67x ITS 1.26M 30-DAY AVERAGE - THE WEAKEST PARTICIPATION OF ANY NAME I AM ADDING TODAY - and the stock traded a narrow 51.11 to 52.04 range and closed at 51.94, which is a name nobody is trading rather than a name being accumulated on a supply shock. That is the single fact most arguing against this position. At 32.05x trailing earnings it is the second most expensive multiple in today's book despite being a shipping asset owner, and 2.70x book on vessels that are marked to a cyclical charter market is not a floor. The deeper problem with the thesis is that Golar's FLNG economics are governed by long-dated tolling agreements on specific vessels - Hilli and the newbuild programme - so a spot LNG price spike accrues largely to cargo owners rather than to Golar's tolling fee, which means the equity moves on narrative here more than on near-term cash flow, exactly the criticism this book has already levelled at its Cheniere position. Golar is Bermuda-domiciled with a concentrated shareholder base and a history of complex spin-offs and related-party transactions. At a $5.28B market cap on an 85.2M float it is small and illiquid relative to everything else here. And it is the fifth position in this book that fails on a Gulf de-escalation headline. Overnight only.

positions.name: Adobe Inc.
positions.exitRule: Intraday - flat by the 9/10 close, BEFORE the after-hours FQ3 earnings release
positions.driver: Tier 2: FQ3 report after the 9/10 close, $5.84 EPS consensus - trade the drift, exit before the print
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 PRE-EARNINGS DRIFT INTO A REPORT THAT LANDS TONIGHT, EXPLICITLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY EXITED BEFORE THE PRINT: Adobe reports FQ3 after the close on 9/10 with a $5.84 EPS consensus, and it is quoted at 255.82 against a 254.86 close, +0.38%. The trade is the day's positioning bid, not the event: I take the drift and am flat by the 4pm close, carrying zero exposure to the release. The structural argument for owning it for one session is valuation rather than momentum - at 14.71x trailing earnings Adobe is the CHEAPEST name in this entire book on a P/E basis apart from the tankers, and it sits 31% below its 370.86 52-week high from 9/18/2025 after a year in which the market has priced generative AI as an existential threat to its creative franchise. A stock that has already been de-rated by a third going into a print has an asymmetry that a name at a 52-week high does not, and expectations are correspondingly low. It is also the second Technology Services name, a sector at two of a possible four, which is the diversification this book badly needs against nine energy- and defence-levered positions.
positions.risks: THE DRIFT IS ACTUALLY NEGATIVE AND I AM CALLING THAT OUT AS THE PRIMARY OBJECTION: Adobe opened 9/9 at 258.06, ran to 259.43, fell to 254.40 and closed at 254.89 - AT THE LOW OF ITS RANGE, down 1.2% - on 4.17M shares against a 4.37M 30-day average (0.95x). A pre-earnings setup wants positive drift into the event and this one closed on its low the session before. The +0.38% quote this morning is a bounce off that weak close, not confirmation, which makes this the WEAKEST-EVIDENCE POSITION IN TODAY'S BOOK and I am taking it primarily because the tape offered so few named catalysts on a morning when almost everything outside energy was quoted lower. Pre-earnings drift is the flimsiest catalyst category available - it is a positioning observation, not information - and this book's own AVAV position proved it 24 hours ago: bought on the same logic at 150.39, it fell 5.4% through the session and was closed at 140.80 for a 220.57 loss. AEO beat EPS by 193% overnight and is quoted DOWN 14.9%; COO beat and is quoted DOWN 16.5%. The 14.71x multiple is cheap because the market genuinely believes generative AI is compressing Adobe's pricing power, and a cheap multiple has been a value trap in this name for four straight quarters. THE ENTIRE VALUE OF THIS SETUP DEPENDS ON THE 4PM EXIT BEING EXECUTED - if it is not, this position carries an unhedged earnings gap into a print, and the next scheduled run of this book is tomorrow morning. Flat by the 9/10 close, no exceptions.
